method: OPEN AND QUOTED, from the RCH Melbourne Clinical Practice Guideline 'Hydrocarbon poisoning' (Last updated June 2017), retrieved 2026-09-23. Every pass claim is machine re-checkable. LICENCE: Free to read but NOT openly licensed -- each page carries '(c) 2026 The Royal Children's Hospital'. Quoted with attribution on the same footing as the 14 RCH guidelines and the Immunisation Handbook guidelines already in this compendium.

claims.claim: **CNS, respiratory and cardiac effects are the main concern.**
claims.source_text: CNS, respiratory and cardiac effects are of main concern
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Hydrocarbon poisoning' (Last updated June 2017), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Hydrocarbon_poisoning/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Inhalation injury may appear up to 6 hours after exposure.**
claims.source_text: Inhalation injury may manifest up to 6 hrs after exposure
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Hydrocarbon poisoning' (Last updated June 2017), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Hydrocarbon_poisoning/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Less than 5 mL of pure essential oil can cause significant CNS toxicity in children.**
claims.source_text: Ingestion of less than 5 mL of pure essential oil can lead to significant CNS toxicity in children
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Hydrocarbon poisoning' (Last updated June 2017), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Hydrocarbon_poisoning/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Hydrocarbons can cause rapid-onset CNS depression and seizures**; volatile hydrocarbons can be aspirated and cause **chemical pneumonitis**. Dysrhythmias are less common.
claims.source_text: Hydrocarbons can cause rapid onset of CNS symptoms including CNS depression and seizures. Volatile hydrocarbons can be aspirated and cause chemical pneumonitis. Cardiac dysrhythmias are less common
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Hydrocarbon poisoning' (Last updated June 2017), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Hydrocarbon_poisoning/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Exposure is accidental (often younger children) or deliberate (often inhaled — 'sniffing' or 'chroming').**
claims.source_text: Poisoning can occur from accidental exposure (often younger children) or deliberate exposure (often from inhalation eg from “sniffing” or “chroming”)
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Hydrocarbon poisoning' (Last updated June 2017), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Hydrocarbon_poisoning/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Sources:** petrol, kerosene, lighter fluid, paraffin oil, 2-stroke fuel, diesel, solvents, white spirit, lubricating oil, furniture polishes, essential oils, mineral turpentine.
claims.source_text: Sources: Petrol Kerosene Lighter Fluid Paraffin Oil 2 Stroke Fuel Diesel Fuel Solvents White Spirit Lubricating Oil Furniture Polishes Essential oils Mineral Turpentine
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Hydrocarbon poisoning' (Last updated June 2017), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Hydrocarbon_poisoning/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Assess:** all deliberate self-poisoning or significant accidental exposure · any symptomatic child · any child whose developmental age does not fit accidental poisoning.
claims.source_text: All patients with deliberate self-poisoning or significant accidental exposure Any symptomatic patient Any patient whose developmental age is inconsistent with accidental poisoning as non-accidental poisoning should be considered.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Hydrocarbon poisoning' (Last updated June 2017), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Hydrocarbon_poisoning/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **History:** intent · type of compound · quantity ingested · duration of any inhalation · co-ingestants such as paracetamol.
claims.source_text: Was exposure intentional or accidental? … Type of compound Quantity ingested Duration of exposure in inhalation Co-ingestants (eg paracetamol)
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Hydrocarbon poisoning' (Last updated June 2017), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Hydrocarbon_poisoning/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Coughing, gagging or choking means aspiration.** Wheeze, tachypnoea, hypoxia, haemoptysis and pulmonary oedema signal evolving chemical pneumonitis.
claims.source_text: Coughing / gagging / choking indicates aspiration Wheeze, tachypnoea, hypoxia, haemoptysis and pulmonary oedema are signs of evolving chemical pneumonitis.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Hydrocarbon poisoning' (Last updated June 2017), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Hydrocarbon_poisoning/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Dysrhythmias occur early.** CNS depression, coma and seizures may follow large acute exposures, **usually within 2 hours.**
claims.source_text: Dysrhythmias occur early in exposure … CNS depression, coma and seizures may occur with large acute exposures. Onset is usually within 2 hours
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Hydrocarbon poisoning' (Last updated June 2017), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Hydrocarbon_poisoning/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Asymptomatic child, small ingestion: usually no investigation.** Significant ingestion or symptoms: **12-lead ECG and cardiac monitoring for 4 hours**, FBE, UEC, LFTs, VBG, and CXR if respiratory symptoms.
claims.source_text: Asymptomatic children with small ingestions do not usually require investigation. For children with more significant ingestions, or who are symptomatic: 12 lead ECG & cardiac monitoring for 4 hours FBE, UEC, LFTs, VBG CXR if respiratory symptoms
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Hydrocarbon poisoning' (Last updated June 2017), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Hydrocarbon_poisoning/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Deliberate poisoning:** screen for co-ingestants — BSL and paracetamol level.
claims.source_text: For all children with deliberate poisoning, perform further screening for co-ingestants … BSL Paracetamol level
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Hydrocarbon poisoning' (Last updated June 2017), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Hydrocarbon_poisoning/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Supportive care; intubate early for progressive CNS depression.**
claims.source_text: Standard procedures and supportive care Intubate early for progressive CNS depression
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Hydrocarbon poisoning' (Last updated June 2017), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Hydrocarbon_poisoning/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Ventricular dysrhythmias:** advanced life support · intubate, hyperventilate and correct hypoxia · correct electrolytes · **withhold catecholamine inotropes if possible.**
claims.source_text: Ventricular dysrhythmias: Commence advance life support … Intubate, hyperventilate, correct hypoxia Correct electrolyte disturbances Withhold catecholamine inotropes if possible
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Hydrocarbon poisoning' (Last updated June 2017), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Hydrocarbon_poisoning/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Seizures: benzodiazepines first line; avoid phenytoin.**
claims.source_text: Seizures – Benzodiazepines remain standard first line treatment. Phenytoin should be avoided.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Hydrocarbon poisoning' (Last updated June 2017), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Hydrocarbon_poisoning/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Chemical pneumonitis is managed supportively** (oxygen, bronchodilators, NIV or intubation if severe). **No corticosteroids or prophylactic antibiotics**; fever is common after aspiration, so **withhold antibiotics until there is objective evidence of bacterial infection.**
claims.source_text: Chemical pneumonitis is managed supportively (Oxygen & bronchodilators – may require non invasive ventilation or intubation if severe). Corticosteroids and prophylactic antibiotics are not indicated. Fever is common following aspiration with pneumonitis – antibiotics should be withheld until there is objective evidence of bacterial infection
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Hydrocarbon poisoning' (Last updated June 2017), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Hydrocarbon_poisoning/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Activated charcoal is specifically contraindicated:** it does not bind hydrocarbons and increases aspiration risk.
claims.source_text: Activated charcoal is specifically contraindicated in hydrocarbon poisoning as they do not bind hydrocarbons and increase the risk of hydrocarbon aspiration
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Hydrocarbon poisoning' (Last updated June 2017), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Hydrocarbon_poisoning/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Asymptomatic with normal vital signs: observe 6 hours after exposure before discharge.** Milder respiratory or CNS symptoms: admit for longer observation ± supportive care.
claims.source_text: Asymptomatic children with normal vital signs should be observed for 6 hours post exposure before discharge Patients with milder respiratory or CNS symptoms should be admitted for a longer period of observation +/- supportive care
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Hydrocarbon poisoning' (Last updated June 2017), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Hydrocarbon_poisoning/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Consider admission for all adolescents with an intentional overdose.** Poisons Information: 13 11 26.
claims.source_text: Admission should be considered for all adolescent patients with an intentional overdose. … Consult Contact Victorian Poisons Information Centre 13 11 26 for advice
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Hydrocarbon poisoning' (Last updated June 2017), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Hydrocarbon_poisoning/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **CNS depression, seizures or dysrhythmia → paediatric intensive care.** PIPER: 1300 137 650.
claims.source_text: Patients with CNS depression / seizures or dysrhythmia should be managed in a paediatric intensive care unit … call the Paediatric Infant Perinatal Emergency Retrieval (PIPER) Service: 1300 137 650.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Hydrocarbon poisoning' (Last updated June 2017), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Hydrocarbon_poisoning/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Discharge criteria:** normal GCS · normal ECG · no cough, dyspnoea or wheeze · normal observations including oximetry · observation period complete · after deliberate ingestion, low assessed risk of further self-harm.
claims.source_text: Discharge Criteria Normal GCS Normal ECG No respiratory symptoms (cough, dyspnoea, wheeze) Normal observations including pulse oximetry Period of observation as above For deliberate ingestion a risk assessment should indicate that the patient is at low risk of further self harm in the discharge setting
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Hydrocarbon poisoning' (Last updated June 2017), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Hydrocarbon_poisoning/, retrieved 2026-09-23
